findings.title: Once a card's delivery event leaves the 100-event window, every casual implementer turn discards the verdict and starts a new review run, without bound
findings.description: Whether a turn delivered nothing new is decided only by comparing the implementer's latest agent in_review event on board.events with judgedDelivery(job). BoardStore.event (server/store.ts:597) keeps only the newest 100 events per card. When the delivery event is trimmed, `delivery` is undefined and the check at line 235 never matches. A reopened job then gets rounds = 0 (line 238), so the turn starts a new review with deliveryEvent = undefined. The new verdict then records reviewedEvent = undefined, so judgedDelivery stays undefined and every later casual turn reviews again. maxReviewRounds no longer bounds this, because of the round-2 reset on reopen. The same happens when the card reached In review without an agent delivery event (a person moved it there during the implementer's turn), and once for d143a86 jobs that have a verdict but no deliveryEvent.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not rely on the trimmed log for the verdict identity. Record the delivery on the job when it is judged (e.g. the delivery id or time in apply's review/deliver cases, or a latestDelivery field set when the agent's in_review event is written). Or treat 'no delivery event found' as nothing new when the job already has a verdict and no newer agent status change. Alternatively, exempt the latest agent in_review event per card from trimming.

findings.title: A create that never produced a session turns the documented 'waits for a person' state into failed/session_unavailable on the next pass
findings.description: create() records implementerId/reviewerId (line 743) before agents.create. When the create's outcome is unknown, or it fails with a provider limit until the cooldown budget is used up, waitForPerson (line 850) moves the job to needs_human and drops pendingOp and the instruction, as AUTOMATION-SPEC §4.4 requires. The next reconcile skips the stale-recovery branch (needs_human), refreshes the recorded id, gets agent:null, and calls sideEffectFailed(SessionGone). That closes the job as failed/session_unavailable. The installed daemon's handleFetchAgent returns agent:null, not an error, for an unknown id. The spec says the job waits until a person replies in the recorded session or chooses Run again, and the drawer text says 'reply in the session'. Instead the state lasts one pass. In the unknown-outcome case, if the daemon finishes the slow create after that pass, a full-access session runs the start prompt on a card whose job reads failed. Its turns match no job, so nothing supervises or reviews them.
findings.suggested_fix: For needs_human jobs with code interrupted or cooldown whose session was never confirmed (no turn and no successful create), do not treat agent:null as gone. Keep them waiting, or fail only on a person's action or after an explicit grace period. Alternatively, mark the job when the session is confirmed (create's final transaction, or turnStarted) and apply the SessionGone conversion only to confirmed sessions.

findings.title: subCardActive explores every blocker path with no memoization, and the new :moving/:held suffix runs it again for every queued child on every pass
findings.description: Each recursive call gets `new Set(seen)`, which detects cycles but is not memoization. The walk visits every simple path through queued, not-ready blockers, and each visit calls readiness/linksOf over the whole board. Round 2 made the walk follow non-sibling blockers too. It also made subCardSignature call subCardActive for every queued child (line 284), so parentShouldWake (line 297, plus the signature at 298) roughly doubles the work. wake() repeats parentShouldWake and the signature. tick() runs this for waiting parents on every pass: the 15 s timer, and now every managed turn end. All of it is synchronous CPU in the plugin worker, so board RPCs and hooks stall while it runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Memoize per board snapshot: a Map<taskId, boolean> shared across one parentShouldWake/subCardSignature/turnDecision evaluation, with in-progress nodes treated as not moving to end cycles. That makes each evaluation linear in cards plus links. Also compute linksOf/readiness from a prebuilt index instead of rescanning links for each node.

findings.title: A reviewer verdict submitted during a casual implementer turn mid-review is refused, and the reviewer is then re-sent round 1 for the same delivery
findings.description: The statemachine-5 fix reopens a job under review as soon as the implementer starts any turn: role becomes implementer and the verdict is deleted. submitReview accepts a verdict only while role is reviewer (line 486), so a reviewer finishing its review of the current delivery during that turn gets REVIEW_CLOSED. When the casual turn ends with no new delivery, apply starts review round 1 again on the same delivery and queues a fresh review prompt. The reviewer receives it when its turn ends and must redo a review it already finished.
findings.suggested_fix: While a reopened job has no new delivery yet, accept a verdict whose deliveryEvent is still the implementer's latest delivery (and record it on that delivery). Or delay the reopen of a live review until the implementer's turn actually changes the card (a delivery or a work report) instead of at turn start.

findings.title: A reserved create_card retry still expires after 15 minutes, so the orphaned workspace can't be adopted and a new request makes a second one
findings.description: Round 2 treats a reserved create_card request as an already-checked decision: when the same request is retried, makeCard skips the signed-revision check (`authorizeCardCreation(before, actor, { revision: !reserved })`, line 198). It still calls `this.fresh(issuedAt)` at line 172, though, which refuses any request issued more than 15 minutes earlier. The orphan notice (agent-card-guard.ts:87-88) tells the agent to "retry this same request to reuse it". Almost every refusal after provisioning needs a person to fix it (parent archived or finished, ancestor cancelled, blocker archived). Retries inside the window are refused before provisioning, so by the time a person has fixed the cause, the 15-minute window counted from get_task has usually passed. The retry then always fails with REQUEST_EXPIRED plus the same advice. The agent's only way forward is a new request. That request has a new operationId, so it gets a new Paseo idempotency key and provisions a second workspace. The first workspace's notice stays on the old request's receipt, and no later result mentions it.
findings.suggested_fix: Exempt a request that already has a create_card reservation from fresh() as well: it passed freshness when it was reserved, the same reasoning used to skip the revision check. Alternatively, have the next create_card from the same actor card report outstanding orphan notices, or change the notice text after expiry so it no longer advises a retry that cannot succeed.

findings.title: get_task handoff budget charges a card twice when it is both a sub-card and a blocker, and can replace its fitting evidence with "Omitted"
findings.description: linkExtras works per link view, not per card. linksOf returns one view per link, so a sub-card that also has a `blocks` link to its parent appears twice in `wanted` (relation sub_card and relation blocked_by). The link rules allow that pair: a child-blocks-parent link does not form a cycle. Each view subtracts the card's evidence from the shared 16,000-character budget. Each view also calls `handoffs.set(id, ...)`, so the second view overwrites the first. When the first view fit and the second does not, the card's full evidence is replaced by the "Omitted" sentence. Both link entries in the response then carry the same handoff, so emitted evidence can exceed the stated budget for cards that do fit.
findings.suggested_fix: De-duplicate `wanted` by card id before budgeting, keeping the first view after sorting, or skip a card already present in `handoffs`.

findings.title: Dependency starts now run git status in the parent card's live workspace, which can make the parent agent's own git commands fail on index.lock
findings.description: Round 2 (3aeb420) added the "Parent integration branch" to dependency-ready starts by calling cardHandoff on the parent. cardHandoff calls readHead, which runs `git status --porcelain` in the parent's workspace through defaultGit, without GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0. git status refreshes the index opportunistically and holds `.git/index.lock` while it does. The pre-existing callers read idle workspaces (Done blockers, settled sub-cards). This call targets the parent, which is typically mid-turn: such starts are triggered right after the parent accepts a blocker sub-card, and its next steps are merges and commits in that same checkout. get_task was moved off git status in the same round for this cost reason; this path still uses it.
findings.suggested_fix: For the parent, read only the branch (the stored HEAD, or `rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` as linkExtras' liveBranch does) instead of the full cardHandoff. Or set GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 / `--no-optional-locks` for the read-only status calls.

findings.title: Orphan adoption relies on an idempotency key that includes the resolved base branch; a retry after the root's branch changes makes a second workspace and drops the first notice
findings.description: Round 2's orphan recovery depends on a same-request retry hitting the same Paseo idempotency key. The key's `intent` hash includes `baseRef` as resolved at call time: with no explicit baseRef, that is the project root's current named branch (resolveWorktreeBaseRef). If the root's branch changes between the refused attempt and the retry, the key differs and Paseo provisions a second workspace. The new round-2 code then hides the first one. A successful commit runs `delete receipt.notice` (line 667), and a second failed attempt overwrites the notice with the new workspace id (keepOrphan, line 691). After that, ws-1 is never reported.
findings.suggested_fix: For agent requests, record the resolved baseRef (or the full idempotency key) on the reservation at the first provisioning and reuse it on retries. At minimum, do not delete or overwrite a notice that names a different workspace than the one just saved.

findings.title: flowly_create_card description still says start=later cards are started with flowly_update_card, which refuses separate cards
findings.description: Commit 07e817b fixed the create_card result message for subCard=false start=later ("A person starts it with Run with agent; this card's agent can start only its direct sub-cards"). The tool description agents read was not updated: it still says "start=later parks it in Backlog until you start it with flowly_update_card", and flowly_update_card answers NOT_PARENT for separate cards. The same description says "Repeating the same call returns the same card". Since round 2, a retry after that card was deleted gets REQUEST_REUSED ("This request already created a card, which was deleted since").
findings.suggested_fix: Say "start=later parks it in Backlog: a sub-card you start later with flowly_update_card action=start; a separate card is started by a person (Run with agent)". Qualify the repeat sentence: "returns the same card while it exists".

findings.title: automation-review.md lists two items as not fixed that 07e817b fixed
findings.description: The round-2 docs pass (d4885a4) was written before 07e817b. Its "Not fixed" section is now false on two points. (1) subcards-1, second suggestion: the create_card result for subCard=false start=later no longer says "Start it later with flowly_update_card action=start" (agent-service.ts:229). (2) subcards-4: flowly_update_card action=start now refuses with ANCESTOR_FINISHED through refuseAbandonedTree (agent-service.ts:273), and abandonedAncestor is used through refuseAbandonedTree and authorizeCardCreation. The doc still says a parent under a cancelled or archived ancestor can start its own sub-cards. The section is presented as the list of deliberate open limits, so readers and later reviewers act on wrong information.
findings.suggested_fix: Move both items to Fixed (07e817b) in the Round 2 section. Keep only the parts still open, such as the create_card tool description noted above.

findings.title: A failed job comes back into Needs attention once the person's take-back move is pruned from the card's 100-event history
findings.description: Round 2 (c9807b0) clears a failed job's attention entry only by finding a non-AUTO `status_changed` event after `job.updatedAt` in the card's events. The store keeps only the latest 100 events per card (server/store.ts:597, `if (relevant.length > 100)` drops the oldest), and every managed turn adds at least two lifecycle events. Nothing on the job records the take-back: `cardMoved` ignores failed jobs, so the job keeps the same state and `updatedAt`. Once the person's move falls out of the window, `automationNeedsYou` returns true again. The spec (AUTOMATION-SPEC §6.4) says the entry leaves Needs attention.
findings.suggested_fix: Record the take-back on the job itself. For example, `cardMoved` could set a `takenBackAt` or `acknowledged` field on a failed job when a person moves the card, or settle it as `stopped/card_moved`. The client should then read that field instead of searching the capped event log.

findings.title: A casual answer no longer keeps the verdict once the judged delivery event is pruned: every later implementer turn starts a new paid review round
findings.description: The round-2 rule that a verdict belongs to the delivery it judged (`judgedDelivery`, `reviewedEvent`) recognises 'nothing new' only by finding that delivery event among the card's events: `delivery && delivery.id === judgedDelivery(job)`. The store keeps 100 events per card. When the judged delivery event is pruned, `delivery` is undefined, so the check is skipped. A reopened job also resets its rounds (`rounds = job.reopened ? 0 : ...`), so the turn becomes `review` with no delivery. After that, `deliveryEvent` and `reviewedEvent` are undefined, and every later casual turn starts yet another review cycle at round 1. It never ends as review_rounds. This breaks AUTOMATION-SPEC §4.2: 'the card still stays on the delivery that got the verdict (a casual answer) → the verdict is kept, delivered'.
findings.suggested_fix: Treat a missing delivery event as nothing new when the job already has a judged delivery: `if (judgedDelivery(job) && (!delivery || delivery.id === judgedDelivery(job))) return deliver`. Better, keep the judged delivery's time (`reviewedAt`) on the job and count only agent→in_review events newer than it as new work, or exempt delivery events from the per-card pruning.

findings.title: Board Run lock reads a workspace list up to 15 s old, so freshly created agent cards show Run with agent disabled
findings.description: The round-2 board lock treats 'resources loaded and the card's workspace missing' as unavailable. `resources` refetches only every 15 s, plus on refresh() after a person's own create. A card created by an agent's flowly_create_card, or from another device, appears through the board query first, while the cached workspace list does not yet hold its new workspace. The drawer reads a fresh per-card workspace query, so the two disagree.
findings.suggested_fix: Do not lock cards newer than the last resources fetch (compare `task.createdAt` with `resources.dataUpdatedAt`). Alternatively, refetch resources when the board shows a card whose workspace is unknown, and lock only after that fetch.

findings.title: Drawer reason lines name the wrong cause for two round-2 settlements (workspace gone, take-over)
findings.description: Round 2 reuses existing codes for new causes, but the reason table has no wording for them. `workspaceGone` closes a queued or waiting job as failed/session_unavailable, which shows 'The agent's session is no longer available', although the job may never have had a session and the cause is the card's workspace. A take-over closes as stopped/card_moved, which shows 'The card was moved', although nobody moved the card. Only the activity note says 'Another session took over the card'. The same `card_moved` wording appears when reconcile stops a sub-card because an ancestor was cancelled or archived, and that close records no activity at all.
findings.suggested_fix: Give these settlements their own codes (for example `workspace_unavailable`, `taken_over`, `ancestor_finished`) with translated reasons in all 9 catalogs. Or set the reason from the job detail in these cases, and record an activity event for the reconcile close.

findings.title: occupancy() now fetches the full workspace list for every in-play job on each start and wake attempt
findings.description: Round 1 resolved another card's directory only for jobs that actually held a slot or a running session. Round 2 resolves `directory()` for every other job whose card is still in play (delivered, stopped and failed ones included) before checking whether it holds anything. Each `workspaces.ref(id).refresh()` is a paginated `fetchWorkspaces` scan. A queued card that stays 'occupied' is planned again on every pass: every 15 s, plus every turn end of any managed session and every card move. Each pass then sends K concurrent full-list RPCs to the daemon, which also serves the user.
findings.suggested_fix: Filter candidate jobs by the cheap hold test first: slot states, or jobs with an activeAgent. Then fetch the workspace list once per occupancy call and resolve all directories from it, instead of one `refresh()` per workspace.
